handoff.summary: Install-hardening initiative: IH-2 (ledgercheck schema gate) and IH-3 (socom adopt one-shot) both DONE, pushed, CI green. IH-4..IH-6 remain.
handoff.done:
Two install-hardening items closed this session, each reviewer-ACCEPTed from clean context and CI-verified green.
**IH-2 — ledgercheck run-ledger schema gate** (commit 0fb5298; CI run 27720305663 success). The run ledger (.socom/ledger/runs.jsonl), the #6f measurement spine, was validated by NOTHING — a valid-JSON-but-schema-invalid row (missing verdict, gate_band:"purple") silently mis-scored the eval gate. New tests/ledgercheck.py validates every row against schemas/ledger.xml (8 required keys + 2 enums + 3 int-typed, bool excluded), parsing the field contract FROM the schema (single source). Absent ledger PASSES (fail-open), bad row FAILS (fail-closed). Wired into medium+full+CI (all 3 adapters, via compile). Reviewer ACCEPT 8/8.
**IH-3 — socom adopt one-shot** (commit 87e0351; CI run 27721993533 success). A fresh clone's LOCAL git gates were dormant: core.hooksPath was only PRINTED as a manual step (auto-healed only inside precond), so pre-commit/pre-push slept until something healed them. New `socom adopt` composes init -> compile -> wire hooks -> report rung in one idempotent command. The .githooks wiring truth was a bare literal in 5+ sites; collapsed to one HOOKS_DIR constant + one _wire_hooks writer, with doctor/precond/adoption_rung reading via _git_hooks_path (only ONE core.hooksPath write site remains). Non-git dir warns to stderr (CI re-asserts), never crashes. README "From a clone" documents BOTH paths (socom installed separately + in-repo ./bin/socom). +7 smoke checks. Reviewer ACCEPT 8/8 (precond heal vs --no-heal preserved; repo_root no walk-up in non-git dir).
Evidence (both, re-run after final edits): the checks.full chain — smoke.sh then xmlcheck.py then ledgercheck.py then `socom index` then echo full-ok -> exit 0; socom doctor . -> rc 0; pre-commit + pre-push gates PASS; 130+ smoke checks green including 5 ledgercheck + 7 adopt.
handoff.undone: Install-hardening initiative remainder (OPEN, leashed in EXTRACTION-BACKLOG.md): - IH-4 (NEXT) — ledger concurrency + chunks.jsonl churn posture. Two parts: (a) _append_ledger_row does read-all-then-append with no flock/lockfile, so two seats recording at once lose/interleave a row and race _next_attempt — multi-agent is the stated goal, so this is the gating item before fan-out; (b) .socom/index/chunks.jsonl churns on every `socom index` (committed as documented churn) — decide its posture (gitignore vs deterministic emit vs commit-on-closeout). - IH-5 — `socom update` (version + reconcile local canon edits, GSD manifest model; promote doctor's hash-divergence detector into it). - IH-6 — secrets/PII redaction write-time gate for handoffs (SECRET_RX exists in index/hydrate; extend it). Plus deferred Akili halves: #4 LLM introspection, #6f-3 per-contract cycle metrics, #7b .gitmessage template. And the CI Node-24 action-version bump.

handoff.warnings: - IH-4 is now the gating item before any multi-agent fan-out: the ledger is guarded (IH-2) but NOT concurrency-safe — _append_ledger_row has no lock. Do not run two seats recording to the ledger concurrently until IH-4 lands. - .socom/ledger/runs.jsonl still does not exist (created lazily). ledgercheck PASSES on absence by design; the moment any agent records a row it is live, and a malformed row will RED medium/full/CI (intended). - .socom/index/chunks.jsonl churns on every `socom index` (pre-push full + compile). Committed as documented churn; IH-4 owns the posture decision. Do not hand-edit it. - CI carries the known Node-20 -> Node-24 forced-runtime deprecation annotation (commit b28ada4). Still green; bump actions/checkout + actions/setup-python at the canon root soon. - Hand-filled handoffs must NOT paste raw shell operators into prose: the ampersand and angle-bracket characters are illegal in XML text and xmlcheck (which gates closeout) REDs on them. Describe commands in words, not symbols. (Bit the IH-2 closeout, and the first draft of THIS one — describe, never paste.)
